thread:
alex: Heads-up — customers in prod-us-east-1 are hitting 502/504s on hosted inference since ~11:02am PST. Multiple tickets about timeouts and gateway errors. Suspect autoscale/scale-up lag (HPA + KEDA) combined with model warmup delays. Escalating to oncall.

jamie: Oncall here. Any deploys in the last hour? Which endpoints are failing?

alex: No recent deploys. Affected routes: POST /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Symptoms: request accepted by gateway -> queued -> after ~12–18s gateway returns 504. Token/auth logs show request validated then upstream 5xx/timeouts. Some tenants also saw brief auth/billing errors earlier today (billing-bot gave a card-decline for tenant T-102).

chen: Pasted relevant logs below. Looks like readiness probe failures + KEDA scaling delay.
```
kubectl events --namespace prod
ScaledObject/my-model-scaler - warning: keda: no scale action, queue below threshold
HorizontalPodAutoscaler/my-model-hpa - normal: scaling to 0->1 replicas (insufficient metrics)
pod/model-server-zzz - Readiness probe failed: Get \"/health\": net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded)
model-init: loading model gpt-open-6b-quant took 37.8s
pod/model-server-zzz became ready
reverse-proxy: request timeout waiting for backend (elapsed 18.2s)
```

chen: KEDA pollingInterval configured to 30s and cooldown 300s in this namespace; when queue suddenly spikes we see a slow reaction. HPA minReplicas=0 in many configs which causes coldstart.

maria: Customer repro steps from ticket #CS-4421 (customer corpX): 1) call /v1/generate with prompt X -> waits ~15s -> gateway 504. They retried and got success after ~45s. They captured curl:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-6b-quant","input":"hello"}'
# Response: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
```

alex: Repro on our side: same behavior hitting prod-us-east-1 from staging account. Captured proxied logs showing backend init 40s+. Also noticed billing-svc returned transient 402 for one tenant around 10:58 which correlated with a scheduled payment retry. Possible domino: failed billing -> token rejected -> fallback auth path triggered extra latency? Not certain.

jamie: Immediate mitigations we can flip: 1) bump minReplicas for affected services to 1 or 2, 2) reduce KEDA pollingInterval to 5s for the scaler handling request queue, 3) add a smaller warmup model fallback so requests can succeed faster (gpt-open-3b-quant). Anything we can do without a deploy?

chen: We can patch the ScaledObject and HPA immediately (kubectl apply) — that doesn't need a code deploy. Also increase readinessProbe.timeoutSeconds to 60 to avoid false failures while model loads. For long term: prefetch pipeline to init model outside request path.

alex: Action items:
- chen -> apply emergency patch to scaledobject/HPA (minReplicas=1, pollingInterval=5s) and bump probe timeout (ETA 15m)
- jamie -> enable burst dedicated pool for affected tenants (manual toggle) and route their traffic to fallback model (ETA 30m)
- maria -> update CS tickets with repro steps and mitigations, ask impacted tenants if they want immediate migration to dedicated burst (ETA 20m)

chen: Patch applied in prod-us-east-1 (scaledobject + hpa + probe timeout). Observability: queue drained, new pods came up in ~8s after patch. Still watching for regressions.

oncall-bot: Incident updated: severity=high -> in_progress, owners=[chen,jamie], start_ts=2512345678

maria: Customer CS-4421 updated: provided workaround and offered migration to dedicated pool. Customer accepted temporary migration.

alex: Follow-up notes: root cause likely combination of KEDA tuning (long pollingInterval + threshold config) + HPA minReplicas=0 causing coldstarts + strict readiness probe timeout. Billing/auth transient 402 may have exacerbated the queue but not the primary cause. Next steps: schedule a postmortem, adjust default scaler templates to minReplicas=1 for high-latency models, implement model-prefetch during scale-up.

jamie: Thanks team — nice quick mitigation. :thumbsup:

alex: Leaving this thread open for postmortem notes and timeline. Closing once PMM has the summary.
